description:
`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` re-runs itself under `flock "$BUILD_LOCK"`, which passes the lock's file descriptor to the child and every descendant. A descendant that daemonises keeps holding it after the run exits — `sccache` double-forks to PPID 1 and does exactly that — so the lock is never released and the next caller blocks forever against a run that finished long ago.

The lock path is host-wide (`${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/cargo-ci.lock`) and deliberately shared with the sibling just-in-time checkout, whose wrapper carried the same defect (fixed there as jit issue c3a09e0d). A daemon leaked by either repository wedges the other, so both wrappers need the fix.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The build lock is released when a run exits, even when that run leaves a daemonised descendant behind.
- [hard] REQ-02: The lock is still held for the whole duration of a run, so host-wide build serialization is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A run that cannot acquire the lock reports what holds it instead of blocking silently, and a bounded wait ends in a named error distinguishable from the wrapped command's own exit status.
title: cargo-ci build lock survives its run through a daemonising child
